# Hospital Insurance Benefits Entitlement Under 42 U.S.C. § 426

## Subsection (a) - Individuals Over 65 Years

Individuals aged 65+ qualify for hospital insurance benefits if they meet specific criteria. The statute states: "Every individual who—(1) has attained age 65, and (2)(A) is entitled to monthly insurance benefits under section 402 of this title..."

Key eligibility paths include being entitled to Social Security retirement benefits, being a qualified railroad retirement beneficiary, or having qualified government employment that would satisfy requirements if treated as regular employment.

## Subsection (b) - Disabled Individuals Under 65 Years

The provision establishes: "Every individual who—(1) has not attained age 65, and (2)(A) is entitled to, and has for 24 calendar months been entitled to..." disability insurance benefits, child's insurance benefits based on disability, or widow(er)'s benefits based on disability.

**Key requirement:** Disabled individuals must have "been entitled to" the specified benefits "for 24 calendar months" to qualify for hospital insurance coverage. Benefits commence in the twenty-fifth month of entitlement and continue through the month following termination notice or when the person reaches age 65, whichever occurs first.

Benefits commence in the twenty-fifth month of entitlement and continue through the month following termination notice or when the person reaches age 65, whichever occurs first.

# 42 U.S. Code § 1395c - Description of Program

The statute states:

"The insurance program for which entitlement is established by sections 426 and 426–1 of this title provides basic protection against the costs of hospital, related post-hospital, home health services, and hospice care in accordance with this part for (1) individuals who are age 65 or over and are eligible for retirement benefits under subchapter II of this chapter (or would be eligible for such benefits if certain government employment were covered employment under such subchapter) or under the railroad retirement system, (2) individuals under age 65 who have been entitled for not less than 24 months to benefits under subchapter II of this chapter (or would have been so entitled to such benefits if certain government employment were covered employment under such subchapter) or under the railroad retirement system on the basis of a disability, and (3) certain individuals who do not meet the conditions specified in either clause (1) or (2) but who are medically determined to have end stage renal disease."

This provision, originally enacted August 14, 1935, and added by the Social Security Act Amendments of 1965, establishes Medicare Part A coverage for three eligible populations: seniors, disabled individuals, and those with end-stage renal disease.

**SGA Amounts for 2026:**

The monthly amount of earnings deemed to constitute substantial gainful activity (SGA) for statutorily blind people under title II of the Social Security Act will be $2,830 in 2026.

The corresponding amount of earnings for non-blind people with a determined disability under titles II and XVI of the Act will be $1,690.

**How These Amounts Were Calculated:**

For statutorily blind individuals, the 1994 monthly SGA amount ($930) was multiplied by the ratio of the national average wage index for 2024 ($69,846.57) to that for 1992 ($22,935.42), producing $2,832.18, which was then rounded to $2,830.

For non-blind individuals with a determined disability, the 2000 monthly SGA amount ($700) was multiplied by the ratio of the national average wage index for 2024 ($69,846.57) to that for 1998 ($28,861.44), producing $1,694.05, which was then rounded to $1,690.
